steps.text: Cover a baking sheet with foil and spray lightly with cooking spray. Soak bread crumbs in milk in a small bowl for 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add onion; cook and stir until onion has softened and turned translucent, about 5 minutes. Reduce heat to low and continue cooking and stirring until onion is very tender, about 15 minutes more.

Gently stir beef and pork together in a large bowl. Add onions, bread crumb mixture, eggs, Parmesan cheese, parsley, garlic, salt, black pepper, Italian herb seasoning, and red pepper flakes; mix together using a rubber spatula until combined. Cover and refrigerate for about one hour.
Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
Form mixture into balls about 1 ½ inches in diameter; arrange in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until browned and cooked through, 15 to 20 minutes.
Serve with your favorite tomato sauce. Enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Chef John's Italian Meatballs
raw_recipe.description: These Italian meatballs use a delicious mix of ground beef and pork and get added flavor from garlic, Italian herb seasoning, and Parmesan cheese.

video.description: In this video, you’ll learn how to make simple Italian meatballs using both ground pork and beef. Find out why a few cloves of crushed garlic are NOT optional ingredients in this recipe! You’ll see how to avoid over mixing your meatballs and discover the benefit of chilling your meat mixture first before forming balls. Bake your meatballs until browned and then add to your favorite tomato sauce and simmer. Be sure to make some extras for meatball sandwiches! You’ll also learn Chef John’s rule of thumb for determining how much salt to add to ground meat recipes and see what size of meatball is officially sanctioned by Chef John.
video.name: How to Make Italian Meatballs

review.reviewBody: I made Chef John's meatloaf a week or so ago and it was quite tasty which made me excited to try his meatball recipe. The bread crumbs I used in this recipe were made from homemade garlic-butter croutons and I cut back on the salt just a bit. To make uniform meat balls, I used my small cookie scoop. After baking my meatballs, I drained the fat off of them and added them to a homemade marinara and let them sit in the sauce for 20 minutes or so before I served them on pasta. The family really thought these were quite good. They held up well (to both cooking in the oven and sitting in the marinara) and had a nice flavor. Next time, I'd double the italian seasoning but that's really just personal to our family.

These meatballs were awesome! I added more breadcrumbs than the recipe called for, left out the red pepper, and used beef broth instead of milk. They were a big hit and I even posted a picture! Thanks Chef John!

These tasted really good and were super easy to make. Just a couple of things: I think next time I'll use maybe a 1/3 cup of milk as they were almost too juicy to form into balls. Also, next time I will try baking them with a rack in the pan as they really did make a lot of grease and I think they would taste better without sitting in it. Third, I wish they would have browned up a little better. I even kept them in the oven for a few more mintutes at 450 and that didn't help. But, again, the best tasting meatballs I've ever made. Nothing wrong with the recipe as written, just personal preference, a five star recipe for sure!

Wow! So much flavor! Great over spaghetti and sandwiched between garlic bread. Picture is last nights leftovers being reheated :-) We were between this recipe and the Ricotta Meatball recipe Chef John also has, so we opted to add a cup of whole milk ricotta and add a little extra breadcrumb/milk. We didn't have any Italian herb seasoning or crushed red pepper, so we used 1/2 tsp pf herbs de provence, 1/2 tsp of thyme, and about 1/8 tsp each of poultry seasoning and cayenne. We followed Chef Johns portioning recommendation of making each ball just a bit larger than a golf ball and we got 30 meatballs, which we baked for 25 minutes. We used 2 jars of Bertolli Tomato & Basil with olive oil for the simmering sauce and kept the heat really low for an hour (covered). We used an enameled cast iron skillet with deep walls and amazingly, everything fit. The cast iron really holds the heat, so the trick for us was keeping the simmer low enough for the entire hour, so after 20 minutes I actually turned the burner (electric) off and left the pan there for about 10-12 minutes, then rotated the meatballs from the edge of the pan to the center using tongs and turned the burner back on low for another 20-25 and then off again for the remaining time. So fun the make and will be our go-to meatball recipe from now on.

I tried these meatballs for the first time today. I made them exactly according to the recipe like I always do when I try something for the first time. Whenever I am looking for a particular recipe I always try Chef John's first so this was a little disappointing. 

I'd like to make a few comments that others can use or take with a grain of salt (excuse the pun):

1.The red pepper didn't make the meatballs spicy or hot so I 
 wouldn't hesitate to use it again.
2.The meatballs were not "Italian" enough for me so I, like others,
 would increase the Italian spices or use fresh & 4 cloves of 
 garlic would have been better than three.
3.The onions only took about 10 minutes to become transparent. You
 don't want them to brown and taste like "fried" onions so watch
 carefully.
4. The recipe had too much onion and made them taste like
 meatloaf. I would cut back or eliminate next time.
5. I felt 40 smaller meatballs would be better in the sauce. I made
 thirty but they seemed big. 
6. Mine browned only slightly but I didn't keep them in longer as I
 didn't want them to dry out. May try 450 degrees & decrease the 
 time if I decrease size.
7. I used at least 1/2 cup of parsley, pressed down, and it was fine. 

Question: Any tips on how to keep them from going flat on the
 bottom?

All in all a pretty good recipe I will try again. Video shows good instructions for forming and mixing. 

Thanks Chef John.

I have to admit I made 3 changes. I used 1 lb 88 % ground beef and 1 lb mild Italian sausage. Because I did this, I used only 1/2 the red pepper flakes and they have the perfect heat for us. I only had Italian bread crumbs so I used those. So flavorful, moist, and tender. I cooked to 165-170 degrees internal temp(instant read thermometer). Took about 15 minutes in my oven. Mine were about 1 1/2" diameter raw. This made 68 meatballs. Once done, I promptly ate 3 right off the pan! Yum. I couldn't eat just one!

I have been making Chef John’s meatball recipe for several years. Any family gathering except Thanksgiving my meatballs are expected. Especially family coming out of state. I agree with the 80/20 ground beef ratio. A lesser fat content will produce drier meatballs. My only change is using dehydrated onion flakes to the breadcrumb/milk mixture.I also try to make the meatball mixture the day before making/baking them. I pat dry the meatballs of any fat with paper towels. I add the baked meatballs to my homemade tomato sauce and simmer approximately 1 1/2 hours

Amazing. Family loved it and had seconds. I made my own italian spice mix and didn’t have oregano, so I substituted with marjoram, I also added another pound of meat and added another teaspoon of salt to season that extra pound. I also used oats instead of breadcrumbs to make it gluten free. Despite the slight deviations from the original recipe it came out amazing. Oh I also made a pomodoro sauce separately and dropped them in there after they were done in the oven. Dinner was a hit.

The only change I made to this recipe was that I used gluten free bread crumbs in this recipe and I was worried when I went to combine the soaked bread crumbs and found the bread crumb/milk mixture had become a jello-like consistency. I still used it in the recipe but mixed with my hands since I couldn’t combine it we’ll using a spoon. It still combined well, and I continued following the recipe exactly. First time making gluten free meatballs, and first time using this recipe. No doubt these were THE BEST meatballs our family has ever had. Thank you for sharing!

delicious taste. I did add a touch of basil and oregano because I didn't have any italian seasoning. If you're particular about your meat balls being round be sure you refrigerate for over an hour so that you can work well making the balls. Loved it!

Good recipe, I made two key changes though. Don't cook the onions and garlic. Leaving them raw and allow it to cook with the meatballs, now you can actually taste the ingredients and adds som texture also since everything is soft. Also added more of the italian seasonings since many people complained it didn't have enough flavor.

These did not look appetizing, they were a bit gray and oozing cheese and oil, HOWEVER, they tasted phenomenal. Absolutely delicious. Here are my recipe notes: Added a shallot, additional garlic clove (minced all garlic), 1 tsp dried parsley instead of fresh chopped and 1 tsp oregano, 1/2 tsp basil, 1/2 tsp thyme instead of Italian seasoning. Followed recipe to a T. Got 30 meatballs. Meatball temp was Over 160° @ 15 mins on 425°. Next time check at 13 mins. Should take out the oven at 155° for baked rigatoni/flash freezing.

This is my go to recipe for meatballs! The only thing I change is that I use a 4 cheese blend of Asiago, Parmesan, Reggiano and fontina. They come out so juicy. I make mini ones for my Italian wedding soup and stuff larger ones with mozzarella pearls for pasta. So good!

Great recipe! I didn’t have breadcrumbs so just tore up a slice of white bread and soaked them in the beef broth. Forgot to oil the foil before placing the meatballs on the baking sheet, so a couple of meatballs did get a little stuck. No biggie though; they held together really well. Very moist, juicy and flavorful. My husband had his with his tomato pasta sauce, and I had mine in pesto. Definitely recommend this recipe!

I made the recipe "as is" the first time and got 30 meatballs. I just made it again and tweaked it. I used 1 lb Italian sausage and 1 lb ground venison sausage (we have a freezer full). I also used ricotta with some milk to soak the breadcrumbs. The ricotta definitely elevated it! This time, I got 40 meatballs. Both times, I used a lever action ice cream scoop that measured 1.5 tablespoons to ensure uniformity and used the stick-proof aluminum foil.
Did exactly what the recipe said to do. Easy. By far the best Italian meatballs we've ever made at home.

LOVE this recipe and it is my GO TO for meatballs....along with your red sauce. The only change I made (by mistake) was to use sweet Italian sausage. I noticed the recipe calls for ground pork, which I did after I discovered my mistake. It was good, but we prefer the sweet Italian sausage. Also I use at least 1/2 bunch of fresh parsley... DELICIOUS!!!
Only had ground beef which worked out fine. These are pretty easy to make.

I absolutely love these meatballs. I've now made them 3 times. I have put them in spaghetti sauce but for me that only detracts from the wonderful flavor of the meatball. I love them just plane. It's my go to snack in the evening. Just pop them in the microwave for 20 seconds, and it's just like they are fresh out of the oven.

Soaking the breadcrumbs in milk was a first for me and made them lovely and moist and much less dense than previous attempts. I added a desert spoon of natural yoghurt (obviously not necessary but had some in the fridge, could taste it a little in end result, was nice I thought). Was worried my mixture was too wet and the meat would flatten in the oven but kept shape very well, no foil, straight onto oiled baking tray. Overall, agree these are the best meatballs ever, mainly due to the texture. Due to having a lack of patience I hadn't seen the video before hand, so my meatballs were easily twice the size of golf balls and cooked entirely in the oven for 30 minutes and still came out lovely.
